💬 Iran will not compromise its national security, sovereignty, Official says

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Ali Bagheri Kani says the Islamic Republic will not compromise on defending its national security and sovereignty.

Bagheri Kani made the remarks during a meeting with China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing on Monday.
​
“Tehran’s position on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and Iran will make no compromises on these matters,” he said.
​
Bagheri Kani also denounced as an “unforgettable” war crime the illegal US-Israeli aggression against Iran and the assassination of Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, along with his family members, stressing that such atrocities must not be allowed to continue.
​
Highlighting the consequences of the United States’ warmongering and hegemonic ambitions, he said that war against an entire civilization cannot lead to victory and that such an approach would disrupt the global economy.
​
The official also said he had discussed with the top Chinese diplomat Tehran's diplomatic initiatives to end the war, and ways to strengthen lasting security in the region.

🤪 The Chinese CS2 TikTok account is doing its own thing

Remember how chickens were introduced in CS2? Eggs simply started appearing in weekly drops, and they weren’t even mentioned in the patch notes until several days later. In China, however, the promotion of chickens looks completely different, and now some mysterious references have started appearing.

Since the release of the new chicken mechanic, the official Chinese CS account has been regularly posting promotional content about it. Every Wednesday, they remind players to claim their chicken and release a themed video or image to go along with it.

Today, they released a strange poster featuring a reference to Resident Evil, along with the words “Everything is getting out of control.” Some believe it’s just a meaningless promotional poster, while others see it as a hint at a potential new mode similar to Zombie Hunt or an upcoming update that expands the chicken mechanic.

The groom’s exemption

Some 230 Haredi men were due to enter noncombat service Sunday. Outside the induction base, protesters tried to stop them. Elsewhere, politicians demanded that military police release a draft evader because he had just married.

Dozens blocked roads outside Tel Hashomer. Police said they were intimidating recruits, while the army said none was prevented from entering. The confrontation exposed a divide the protest leaders prefer to obscure. Some Haredi men are joining, and others are trying to make that choice harder.

Military police arrested Yaari Lieberman on his way with his wife to a sheva brachot celebration, one of the traditional meals held during the week after a wedding. An earlier arrest attempt ended with his release after hundreds of protesters surrounded his building. This time he received 20 days in military detention.

United Torah Judaism lawmaker Meir Porush called the arrest “criminal conduct” that should shock every Jew. Shas asked fellow lawmakers to demand Lieberman’s release so he could resume celebrating.

The legal basis for blanket yeshiva exemptions ended with the Supreme Court’s 2024 ruling. Political leaders have yet to secure a replacement. For now, they are proposing a more personal exception, in which enforcement waits until the wedding festivities are over.
